heading: Activations
text:
### Activations [IDAT.6.2]

An activation is a rule together with the particular facts that matched it: a
firing that is owed but has not happened yet. It is internal to libds: no
public function takes or returns one ([IARC.6.1]).

The ownership split inside one is what matters. The activation holds a
**non-owning borrow** of each fact it matched, and of its rule, which a
registry that outlives every activation owns. An activation therefore cannot
outlive the facts it matched -- which is why retracting one of them destroys
the activation rather than leaving it holding a dangling reference
([IDAT.6.2.1]).

The agenda orders activations by their rule's ordinal, then their entry order,
the tie-break within a single rule when several partial matches have completed
([RARC.5.4.7], [LDET.5.5]). The fired flag is the refraction state
([IDAT.6.2.2]) and is no ordering key: an activation carrying it is suppressed,
not sorted ([LDET.5.3]).
